summary.text: Heather Boyd is a Democratic state representative who has represented Pennsylvania House of Representatives District 163 since June 5, 2023 and is on the ballot for re-election on November 3, 2026.
Before joining the House she worked as a district director to a member of Congress and as chief of staff to a state representative.

paragraphs.text: Heather Boyd lives in Drexel Hill, Pennsylvania, and graduated from Port Huron Northern High School.
She earned a B.A. in history from the University of Michigan in 1998, an M.A. in art history from James Madison University in 2001, and an M.A. in history from the University of Delaware.

Her career included working as the district director, campaign manager and a senior advisor to Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon, as chief of staff to state Representative Leanne Krueger, and as an instructor with Delaware County Community College.
Boyd served on the Upper Darby School District board as an at-large member from 2015 to 2018, founded the Delaware County Chapter of NOW, and has chaired the Upper Darby Democratic Committee.

In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, Boyd listed public education funding, access to health care, reproductive rights, affordable housing, justice system reform and workers' rights among the policy areas she is passionate about.
She said she is committed to the seven-year school funding plan set out by the Basic Education Funding Commission.
